activities.title: Which chart would you use?
activities.intro: Match each situation to the chart that answers its question best: compare, trend over time, or parts of one whole.

blocks.prompt: Put each situation under the best chart type.
items: Supplies cost per item this month
The office's electricity bill, January to June
How a ₱20,250 household budget is split
Number of staff present per section today

help: Compare items, sections or people: column or bar.
Months, weeks or days in order: line.
Shares that add up to one whole: pie, about 6 slices or fewer.

activities.title: Chart your inventory's Total Cost
activities.intro: This chart counts toward Lab 3, so build it carefully on your real Jan sheet. Then run the self-check.

items: Select A1:A9, hold Ctrl (Mac: Cmd), and select E1:E9.
Insert a Bar or Column chart.
Type a real chart title: what, where, when.
Add axis titles and data labels. Delete the legend.
Move the chart beside the table and resize it until every label reads clearly.

blocks.prompt: Which cells did you select for the chart?
Self-check: which item has the longest bar?
What data label is on the longest bar?
Type the chart title you used.
Optional: a screenshot of your chart

help: A TOTAL bar towers over everything? You included row 10. Select rows 1 to 9 only.
Numbers along the axis instead of item names? Column A was not selected. Hold Ctrl while you add E1:E9.
The default text "Chart Title" does not count as a title in Lab 3. Click it and type a real one.
Excel: the + button beside the chart adds titles and labels. Sheets: Chart editor, Customize. Calc: double-click the chart, then Insert.

blocks.prompt: You select A1:A10 and E1:E10 and insert a pie. One slice is exactly half the pie. Why?
options: Long paper is half of all spending
Row 10, the TOTAL, became a slice
Pie charts always enlarge the first slice
The chart needs a legend to fix it
